keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row). The infobox gives the regencies Luwu, North Luwu, East Luwu and Palopo City; Braam Morris in 1889 'placed Luwu's peak territorial extent between the 10th and 14th centuries, but offered no clear evidence'. No area is given. The disc is the researcher's modern approximation; Luwu's 'peak' extent claim is not drawn.

region.text: northern South Sulawesi: the regencies of Luwu, North Luwu, East Luwu and Palopo City (infobox), the Gulf of Bone coast and foothills where Bugis settled round 1300

ledger.note: c. 1300: the Luwu kingdom is dated. Infobox 'Established ca. 1300'; 'Bugis settlers began to settle along the coastal margins of Luwu around the year 1300 CE'. The page also calls the 10th-14th century estimate from the La Galigo epic doubtful ('Estimated to be founded between the 10th and 14th century, but recent archaeology challenges this').

4-5 February 1605: Luwu becomes a sultanate. Ruler La Patiwareq (Daeng Pareqbung) 'became the first major South Sulawesi ruler to embrace Islam', taking the title Sultan Muhammad Wali Mu'z'hir al-din.

c. 1620: the capital moves from Malangke to Palopo. 'Around 1620, Malangke was abandoned and a new capital was established to the west at Palopo' (the page also cites the economic potential of trade with the Toraja highlands).

region.text: northern South Sulawesi: the regencies of Luwu, North Luwu, East Luwu and Palopo City (infobox), the Gulf of Bone coast and foothills where Bugis settled round 1300

ledger.note: 1905: the Dutch take South Sulawesi. The South Sulawesi expeditions page dates the Dutch occupation of Bone (July 1905) and Gowa (October 1905); the Luwu page says only that 'the Dutch first came to the Kingdom of Luwu during the reign of Andi Kambo (1901-1935)' and dates the abolition to 1954. The year 1905 is the researcher's bridging (page silent).

region.text: northern South Sulawesi: the regencies of Luwu, North Luwu, East Luwu and Palopo City (infobox), the Gulf of Bone coast and foothills where Bugis settled round 1300

ledger.note: 1905: Luwu ends as a sovereign kingdom (bridging, page silent). The line of the Pajung continued: the kingdom's abolition is dated 1954 (infobox 'Dissolution of Sultanate 1954'), and the Pajung Andi Jemma was detained and exiled by the Dutch in 1945-1950.

wars.name: Dewaraja's attacks on Wajo and Sidenreng
wars.outcome: 'Stories current today in South Sulawesi tell of his aggressive attacks on the neighboring kingdoms of Wajo and Sidenreng' (Dewaraja, c. 1495-1520); the page records that 'Luwu's power was eclipsed in the 16th century' and that its defeats are in the Chronicle of Bone.
wars.note: No dated territorial result; the Wajo page has Wajo and Luwu winning a war against Sidenreng in Ajatappareng, undated.

certainty.note: The page gives no frontier for any date; the disc stands for the regencies of the infobox.

notes: Cliopatria has no row for Luwu. Wikidata id not looked up (wikidata.org unreachable): null. The page gives no territory beyond 'the northern part of the modern-day South Sulawesi province' and the four regencies in the infobox; the Toraja highlands, Kolaka, Mengkoka and Pitumpanua are not on the page. The end year 1905 is bridging; the page's own end is 1954 (Pajung line, then the abolition of the kingdoms). A Dutch-vassal tint for 1905-1954 is the dutch-east-indies dossier's to draw. Ruler strip omitted: the page lists reigns (1571-1587 onward) in a table the summariser returned only as year ranges. Gazetteer: Malangke, Palopo area names are not used as places (coordinates).
